objectives.text: Singers can get to their own part quickly before rehearsal
The choir's volunteers spend little time keeping the service running

rejected.label: Syncs with the rehearsal calendar app
rejected.note: Stated as a must. Treated as a way of avoiding volunteer re-entry of rehearsal dates, which is an assumption of mine; it is judged through upkeep-effort, and whether it is a veto is asked.

rejected.label: Dark mode
rejected.note: Nobody raised it as a reason for the decision; it appears only because the brochures list it.

anchors.text: A source states that a singer must open the full score and locate their own part by hand.
A source states that a singer can open a piece and select their voice part from a list.
A source states that a singer's own part opens directly from a saved voice-part setting, without selecting it each time.

definition.objective: Singers can get to their own part quickly before rehearsal
definition.question: How many steps does a singer take from opening the service to seeing their own part of a piece?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's documentation or product page describing how a singer reaches a part; general claims such as 'easy to use' do not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how a singer reaches their own part.
Sources disagree about how a part is reached.

exclusions: How the sheet music looks on screen, including dark mode.
Syncing with the rehearsal calendar app: that is not about finding a part.

anchors.text: A source states that routine upkeep tasks must be done by a volunteer each week.
A source states that routine upkeep tasks are needed monthly or less often.
A source states that the vendor hosts and updates the service so that no routine volunteer task is required.

definition.objective: The choir's volunteers spend little time keeping the service running
definition.question: How often does a volunteer have to do routine upkeep for the service to keep working?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's administration documentation or hosting description; a reviewer's impression of effort does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes routine upkeep or who hosts the service.
Sources disagree about how often upkeep is needed.

exclusions: Syncs with the rehearsal calendar app: judge the volunteer time, not the mechanism.
The price of the service.
The effort of the one-off initial setup.

provenance.quote: Singers need to find their parts quickly before rehearsal.
We can't afford anything that needs a volunteer to maintain it every week.

questions: You said the service must sync with your rehearsal calendar app. It is treated here as a way of reducing volunteer upkeep, but I do not know why it matters to you. What does it achieve for the choir? And is it a hard requirement, so that a service without it is ruled out whatever else it does?
Cost was not mentioned beyond 'can't afford'. Is price a criterion for this decision, or already settled by a budget?
The choice is for three seasons. Does it matter to you whether the service will still be supported and priced as now in later seasons?
Are there other things singers or the committee need from the library (for example adding new pieces, or working without internet at rehearsal)? None were stated, so none were added.

objectives.text: Parts arrive before the competition deadlines
Mentors do not spend their evenings chasing orders

rejected.label: Orders go through the school's purchase-order system
rejected.note: Stated as a must. Treated as a way of keeping ordering simple for volunteer mentors, which is an assumption of mine; it is judged through order-chasing, and whether it is a veto is asked.

rejected.label: Branding
rejected.note: The user said to forget about branding.

rejected.label: Loyalty points and rewards
rejected.note: Nobody raised it as a reason for the decision; it appears only because the brochures list it.

anchors.text: A source states that stocked items are dispatched more than five working days after the order.
A source states that stocked items are dispatched within two to three working days of the order.
A source states that stocked items are dispatched the next working day.

definition.objective: Parts arrive before the competition deadlines
definition.question: How soon after an order is a stocked item dispatched?
definition.evidenceRule: A dispatch time stated in the supplier's delivery or shipping terms; a general claim of 'fast delivery' does not count.

missingRules.when: No source states a dispatch time.

exclusions: Items that are out of stock; that is restock-lead-time.
Time spent in the carrier's hands after dispatch.
Delivery charges.

anchors.text: A source states that out-of-stock items take several weeks to arrive.
A source states that out-of-stock items arrive within one to two weeks.
A source states that an out-of-stock item's delivery date is given when ordering and falls within a week.

definition.objective: Parts arrive before the competition deadlines
definition.question: How long does an item that is not in stock take to arrive, according to the supplier?
definition.evidenceRule: A lead time or restock estimate in the supplier's terms or product pages; forum anecdotes do not count.

missingRules.when: No source states a lead time for out-of-stock items.
The supplier states that every catalogued item is held in stock.

exclusions: Items that are in stock; that is dispatch-speed.
How often items are out of stock.

anchors.text: A source states that order status can only be learned by contacting the supplier directly.
A source states that customers can look up order status in an account.
A source states that customers get automatic status updates and tracking for each order without contacting the supplier.

definition.objective: Mentors do not spend their evenings chasing orders
definition.question: How much must a mentor do to find out where an order is?
definition.evidenceRule: The supplier's documentation of order tracking and notifications; a reviewer's general praise of service does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how order status is communicated.
Sources disagree about tracking or notifications.

exclusions: Orders go through the school's purchase-order system: judge the mentor time, not the mechanism.
How fast parts are dispatched; that is dispatch-speed.

overlaps.probe: Two options are identical except that one is better on how fast stocked items are dispatched. Do you prefer it, or are you indifferent? And the other way round: identical except that one is better on how fast out-of-stock items arrive. Prefer it, or indifferent?

provenance.quote: We need parts to arrive before competition deadlines.
Mentors are volunteers and can't spend evenings chasing orders.

questions: You said everything has to be ordered through the school's purchase-order system. It is treated here as a way of keeping ordering simple for mentors, but I do not know why it matters. What does it achieve? And is it a hard requirement, so that a supplier that cannot be ordered from that way is ruled out whatever else it does?
Price was not mentioned. Is cost a criterion for this decision, or already settled by a budget?
Is the lead time for out-of-stock items something you care about, or do you only order stocked items?
Do you care about product range, quality or compatibility with your kits? None was stated, so none was added.

objectives.text: Members can borrow a tool without waiting days
Every shared tool is accounted for, so nothing goes missing

rejected.label: Has a mobile app
rejected.note: Stated as a need. Treated as a way of letting members borrow without delay, which is an assumption of mine; it is judged through borrow-speed, and whether it is a veto is asked.

rejected.label: Number of languages supported
rejected.note: Nobody raised it as a reason for the decision; it appears only because the brochures list it.

anchors.text: A source states that every borrow needs approval by a society administrator before the member can take the tool.
A source states that a member can reserve a tool in advance and the lender confirms the pickup.
A source states that a member can borrow an available tool immediately, without anyone approving the request.

definition.objective: Members can borrow a tool without waiting days
definition.question: How long does a member wait between asking for an available tool and being able to take it?
definition.evidenceRule: The platform's documentation of the borrowing flow and any approval step; general claims of 'quick' do not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes the borrowing flow.
Sources disagree about whether approval is needed.

exclusions: Has a mobile app: judge the waiting time, not the mechanism.
Whether the tool is physically available; that depends on the society's stock.

anchors.text: A source states that the platform does not record who has a borrowed tool, and members must ask around.
A source states that the lender can see who borrowed each of their tools.
A source states that every member can see, for each tool, who currently holds it and since when.

definition.objective: Every shared tool is accounted for, so nothing goes missing
definition.question: At any moment, can the society see who currently holds a given tool?
definition.evidenceRule: The platform's documentation of loan records and what each user role can see.

missingRules.when: No source describes whether current holders are recorded or visible.
Sources disagree about what is visible.

exclusions: Reminders and chasing of late returns; that is overdue-follow-up.
How quickly a tool can be borrowed; that is borrow-speed.

anchors.text: A source states that loans have no due date.
A source states that loans have a due date and overdue loans are listed for the lender to see.
A source states that borrowers are reminded automatically before the due date and overdue loans are flagged to the society.

definition.objective: Every shared tool is accounted for, so nothing goes missing
definition.question: What does the platform do when a tool is not returned by its due date?
definition.evidenceRule: The platform's documentation of due dates, reminders and overdue handling.

missingRules.when: No source describes due dates or overdue handling.
Sources disagree about reminders or overdue handling.

exclusions: Seeing who holds a tool right now; that is current-holder-visibility.
Charging fees or penalties.

overlaps.probe: Two options are identical except that one is better on showing who holds each tool. Do you prefer it, or are you indifferent? And the other way round: identical except that one is better on following up on overdue tools. Prefer it, or indifferent?

provenance.quote: Members should be able to borrow a tool without waiting days.
We want to know who has which tool so nothing goes missing.

questions: You said the platform needs a mobile app. It is treated here as a way of letting members borrow quickly, but I do not know why it matters. What does it achieve? And is it a hard requirement, so that a platform without it is ruled out whatever else it does?
Cost was not mentioned. Is price a criterion for this decision, or already settled by a budget or free tier?
Is following up on overdue tools something the society wants, or is knowing who holds each tool enough?
What does 'waiting days' mean in practice: approval by an administrator, finding the tool's owner, or something else?

objectives.text: The group has the route the evening before the walk

rejected.label: Exports GPX files
rejected.note: Stated as a must. Treated as a way of getting a route to the group and into their devices or other apps, which is an assumption of mine; it is judged through share-with-group, and whether it is a veto is asked.

rejected.label: Social feed
rejected.note: The user said nobody cares about the social feed.

rejected.label: Badges and achievements
rejected.note: Nobody raised it as a reason for the decision; it appears only because the brochures list it.

criteria.label: Sharing a route with the group

anchors.text: A source states that a shared route can only be opened in the app by people who have an account.
A source states that a leader can send a route to the group as a link that opens in a browser, but sending to many people means repeating the step for each.
A source states that a leader can send a route to the whole group at once, and recipients can open it without an account or installing the app.

definition.objective: The group has the route the evening before the walk
definition.question: How can a leader get a planned route to every member of the group, and what must members have to open it?
definition.evidenceRule: The app's documentation of sharing and what recipients need; marketing phrases such as 'easy sharing' do not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how a route is shared or what recipients need.
Sources disagree about what recipients need.

exclusions: Exports GPX files: judge whether the group can get the route, not the file format.
The social feed or any public posting of routes.
How the route was planned.

provenance.quote: Leaders need to share a route with the group the evening before.

questions: You said the app has to export GPX files. It is treated here as a way of getting a route to the group, but I do not know why it matters. What does it achieve (for example loading routes on members' own devices)? And is it a hard requirement, so that an app without it is ruled out whatever else it does?
What do group members have: smartphones, a particular app, or only email? That decides what counts as sharing well.
Walk leaders also plan routes in the app. Is planning quality (for example maps, elevation, offline use) something you care about? Nothing was stated, so no criterion was added.
Cost was not mentioned. Is price a criterion, or already settled?
